meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have until 4:40, so we'll skip the small talk. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that, and when.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing down that you admit it. Now, on what basis did you give him the zero?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

Show me the note with the date on it, Hale. And "like, being stuck" is not a wrong answer from a seventeen-year-old put on the spot. Did you tell him on November 2 that his mark depended on that conversation?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale, that's what drafting is for. Put the outline and the essay in front of me, side by side, and I'll read them myself. What else do you have?
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Friday at 3 PM comes after Thursday at 8:15, Hale, and Owen sits nothing until I have that promise in writing first. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, no one in his class hears a word. And I still haven't seen the outline or your note, so put them on the table before you ask me to agree to anything.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In our meeting you admitted entering Owen's zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that promise in writing before Owen sits anything, along with copies of your November 2 note and his October 15 outline, and I require that none of this reach his classmates. I expect it in writing before Thursday at 8:15.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet, and she still wants the no-record promise in writing before the rewrite, the matter kept quiet, and to see the note and outline herself.
What moved her: Comparing Owen's dated October 15 outline with the final essay, because it was specific, dated, his own work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: Describing the note and outline without showing them, because she can't weigh evidence she isn't allowed to read.
Try next time: When you bring up the October 15 outline, put it and the essay in front of her right then so she can compare them herself.
